The Newton Decrement of a Joint Fit, With the Verdict on Its Curvature

Source: R/structural.R
joint_reading.Rd

Reads, at a point, how far a joint objective over the coefficients and a structural term's parameters lies above its maximum, and whether the curvature there admits such a reading.

Usage

joint_reading(g, K, keep, own = integer(0))

Arguments

g

The gradient of the joint objective.

K

Its curvature, a matrix as long as g.

keep

The coordinates to read.

own

The coordinates, among those of g, that are the structural term's own parameters.

Value

A list with decrement (NA where it cannot be computed, when ascent is TRUE, and when partial is TRUE and the lower bound is below mode_error_limit()), ascent, ratio, the smallest eigenvalue's magnitude in units of \(\varepsilon\lambda_{\max}\) (NA when there is nothing to read), and partial.

Details

The reading is the Newton decrement \(\tfrac12 g^\top K^{-1} g\) over the coordinates in keep, after three steps taken in this order.

A coordinate whose diagonal of \(K\) is not positive is flat at an edge, with the sign set by rounding, and is left out. If no coordinate has a positive diagonal the curvature is not flat but negative, nothing is left to read, and ascent is TRUE.

The remaining curvature is read for a direction of ascent. If its smallest eigenvalue is below \(-c\,\varepsilon\,\lambda_{\max}\), with \(c\) from curvature_ascent_limit(), the point is not a maximum, no decrement follows from an indefinite matrix, and ascent is TRUE. deficient_coords() is not consulted in that case, because on an indefinite matrix it can name the term's own parameters, and the decrement over the coordinates that remain is then smaller than the distance to the maximum.

Otherwise the matrix is positive semidefinite up to rounding, the coordinates that deficient_coords() names are left out as aliased, and the decrement is computed over the others. A negative decrement is not possible for a positive semidefinite matrix, so it is read as a direction of ascent.

A column of the design that duplicates another is aliased, and its coordinate carries no information because the objective is flat along it. The same holds for no parameter of the term: the curvature of a filter that has exploded is numerically of rank one, and deficient_coords() then names the term's own parameters, which the objective is not flat in. Where it names one of the coordinates in own, the decrement over the others is a lower bound of the decrement over all of them, so it can show that the point is not a maximum and cannot show that it is one: a value above mode_error_limit() is returned and a value below it is replaced by NA, with partial set to TRUE.

See also

curvature_ascent_limit(), alternation_readings(), statmod_certificate(), filter_decrement()
